title: Enforcement action request v1
description: Body of POST /v1/actions. The daemon refuses (structured error, never faked success) rather than partially enforcing. This is the spec's contract sample, schema form.

action_id.description: Caller-unique id, echoed in every response and stored with the kernel evidence. Replaying it is a no-op; reusing it for a different request is a conflict.

kind.description: The enforcement primitive. v1 has exactly three.

ip.description: Target address. Required for xdp_drop and socket_redirect; forbidden for process_interdict. Loopback, multicast, unspecified, link-local and broadcast targets are refused.

port.description: L4 port; only socket_redirect may set it. 0 means absent.

pid.description: Target process id; only process_interdict may set it. 0 means absent.

ttl_seconds.description: Containment lifetime in seconds. Omitted means the daemon default. Refused below the 60 s floor: an enforcement that outlives its reason is a new finding, and a sub-floor TTL is a no-op wearing an enforced badge.

reason.description: Why this enforcement exists — travels with the action and lands in the audit trail. Required; an unexplained kernel state is indistinguishable from compromise.

idempotency_key.description: Caller's dedupe key, e.g. 'xdp_block_ip:203.0.113.7' — the approval pipeline's existing convention. Required.
